hypothesis: Swapping the demonstration bank from 12 generic hardcoded exemplars to 117 domain-specific corpus sets should fix the "semantically-nearest≠instructive" failure seen in exp007 — closer-domain examples should supply the missing coverage judgment that kept prior RAG variants plateaued.
technique: Semantic NLEmbedding retrieval of the k=3 nearest sets from a 117-entry corpus bank (instead of the 12-exemplar generic pool), injected as few-shot demonstrations into the exp011 contrastive prompt base, then a single greedy on-device generate call.
result: Scored 0.280 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet, specPass 100%), the worst result in the positive-RAG family and −0.040 below the exp003/exp011 best (~0.32); rubric atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=3. Coverage stayed pinned at 3 and close-domain demos slightly increased compound questions and reintroduced first-person phrasing, definitively falsifying the "impoverished pool" escape hatch — discarded.
